html:
"Huns" is the map's label, for 700, for the Huns of the North Caucasus, a nomad people on the Caspian plain of today's Dagestan, north of the pass of Derbent.

They were not Attila's people of two centuries before, but writers used the name Huns for many steppe groups. They were close to the Sabirs and lived under the overlordship of the Khazars. An Armenian history tells how their prince Alp Ilitver was converted to Christianity in the 680s by a bishop from Caucasian Albania to the south. After the Arab wars with the Khazars in the 700s, they fade from the record.
